Hi Sara — thanks for signing up and for the clear questions. Short answers up front: we support several integration patterns for GHE behind a firewall, and we can typically demo the best-fit option live. Details below and a suggested demo cadence.

High-level options:
- Self-hosted connector (recommended for strict air-gapped/GHE installs): a lightweight service you run inside your network that forwards events to Redwood over an authenticated outbound channel. This avoids inbound holes in your firewall.
- Reverse proxy / NAT: customers expose a public endpoint through a proxy; we validate TLS and token auth. Works but requires infra changes.
- Polling / periodic sync: limited (not real-time); fine for batch jobs where latency isn't critical.

OAuth vs bot account: OAuth app install provides the smoothest install and scoped permissions; a bot account with deploy key works for read-only use cases, but webhooks/events require a mechanism to reach Redwood (connector or proxy).

Would a 30-minute demo + 15-minute follow-up tech sync work? I attached a short integration checklist that helps us scope any firewall/network steps before the call. Can you share a couple of 30-min windows tomorrow or Wednesday (PDT)?

Hi Sara — Marissa here (AE on the account). Thanks for the detail; great timing.

Priya's right: the self-hosted connector is what most enterprise customers with strict egress rules opt for. Quick notes for your infra team before the demo:
- Connector model: connector makes outbound TLS to Redwood. No inbound ports required.
- Auth: mTLS + token exchange (we'll provide config examples).
- Egress: allow redwood-inference.com over HTTPS (we'll provide IP ranges if you need that for firewall rules).

I'm copying Mateo (solutions engineer) and we can do a 30-min demo focused on installation and webhook flows, followed by a 15-min tech sync for your infra lead. Please accept the calendar invite I just sent (link below) — proposed: Tue 2027-03-22 10:00 - 10:45 AM PDT.
